title: Nine Films. Four Fridays. ₹1,400 Crore on the Line. June Is Bollywood's Most Dangerous Month in Years.
excerpt: After a drought that gave India five major releases in twelve weeks, Bollywood decided to dump nine in four. Trade analysts are panicking. They should be.
body:
Here's a math problem for you. Between January and May 2026, Bollywood released five major Hindi films across twelve weeks. **Dhurandhar 2** ate the entire March quarter alive. **Bhooth Bangla** had April to itself. May split three ways between **Raja Shivaji**, **Pati Patni Aur Woh Do**, and **Chand Mera Dil**. If you were an exhibitor, you had room to breathe.

June is a different animal entirely.

In the next four Fridays, nine major Hindi and pan-India releases will fight for the same screens, the same audiences, and the same opening-weekend slots. According to **Bollywood Hungama**, the combined stakes exceed ₹1,400 crore. Trade veterans are calling it the most competitive month in Bollywood history. They're not wrong. And they're not happy about it.

## Week by Week: A Collision Course

**June 5** already delivered a three-way pileup: **Varun Dhawan**'s **Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai**, **Bobby Deol**'s **Bandar**, and **Ram Charan**'s Telugu juggernaut **Peddi**. HJTIHH opened to ₹7.50 crore and stayed flat on Saturday — collecting roughly ₹15 crore in two days. Solid for a mid-range rom-com, devastating for a David Dhawan finale that needed legs. Meanwhile, Peddi crossed ₹150 crore worldwide in 48 hours and swallowed most of the oxygen in the room.

**June 12** is somehow worse. Four films in a single week: **Imtiaz Ali**'s **Main Vaapas Aaunga** (Diljit Dosanjh, A.R. Rahman, Naseeruddin Shah — the kind of talent stack that makes everything else on the calendar nervous), **Kangana Ranaut**'s 26/11 drama **Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata**, **Manoj Bajpayee**'s **Governor**, and Vikram Bhatt's **Haunted – Echoes of the Past**. Oh, and **Lagaan** re-releases the same day for its 25th anniversary. Five titles sharing a Friday. It's a bloodbath before the lights go down.

> "Now you can't stop anyone. Every producer thinks, '*Main kyun aage jaau?*' But there will be *maara-maari* for screens." — **Taran Adarsh**, trade analyst

**June 19** brings the one everyone's actually tracking: **Cocktail 2** — **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon**, **Rashmika Mandanna**, directed by **Homi Adajania**, backed by Maddock Films. It's the most anticipated Indian film on IMDb right now with a 21% page-view share. The original **Cocktail** turned Deepika Padukone into a superstar in 2012. The sequel carries that weight, a ₹150 crore budget, and the pressure of being the month's presumptive champion.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZF7BkPjSm7/

**June 26** closes things out with **Welcome to the Jungle** — **Akshay Kumar**, **Suniel Shetty**, **Raveena Tandon**, and **Arshad Warsi** in a multi-starrer comedy betting on franchise nostalgia and holiday-weekend footfalls.

And we haven't even mentioned Hollywood. **Masters of the Universe**, Spielberg's **Disclosure Day**, **Toy Story 5**, and **Supergirl** are all landing in Indian theatres this month, each gunning for premium screens.

## Why the Numbers Don't Add Up

The problem isn't quality — several of these films look genuinely promising. The problem is arithmetic. India has approximately 9,500 screens. A big Hindi release needs 4,000+ screens to open strong. When four films arrive on the same Friday, somebody gets squeezed. Usually, it's the mid-budget film that deserved a clean window but didn't get one.

The irony is that Bollywood's 2026 has been historically top-heavy. **Dhurandhar 2** alone accounts for ₹1,850 crore of the year's ₹3,283 crore worldwide total. Remove it, and the picture is considerably leaner. The industry needed a packed summer to prove the audience hasn't vanished. What it got instead is a cage match where films will cannibalise each other's first weekends.

The 8-week OTT window makes it worse. As **Pinkvilla** noted, the current streaming timeline is conditioning audiences to simply wait for the digital premiere rather than brave the multiplex. Mid-scale films — the rom-coms, the character dramas, the films that used to be Bollywood's bread and butter — are the ones paying the price.

## The Diaspora View

For NRI audiences, June's chaos is actually a gift. Most of these films will get international releases, and the variety is genuinely exciting — from partition romance to 26/11 heroism, from Telugu cricket drama to nostalgia comedy, from Imtiaz Ali's dreamy landscapes to Akshay Kumar's slapstick. There is something for every Sunday-afternoon mood.

The practical advice: if you want **Cocktail 2** opening weekend in the US, book early. If you want **Main Vaapas Aaunga**, book even earlier — Rahman's music alone will fill seats. And if you're the type who roots for the underdog, keep **Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata** and **Bandar** on your radar. They'll need every ticket they can get.

*Buckle up. June has just begun.*
